sentence_stem: Had the team followed the instructions more carefully,
correct_completion: the project would have finished on time.
full_sentence: Had the team followed the instructions more carefully, the project would have finished on time.
acceptable_variants: the project would have been completed on schedule.
the deadline would have been met.

options.text: so the project finished on time.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result that actually happened. The inverted conditional requires a hypothetical outcome, so a past-fact result does not complete it.

options.text: the project would have finished on time.

options.why_wrong: This describes the instructions but does not give the hypothetical result that the conditional stem expects.

options.text: they will follow them next week.
options.why_wrong: The future tense does not match the past perfect condition set up by the stem, which refers to an unreal past situation.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional ('Had' + subject + past participle)
explanation: The inverted form 'Had the team followed' replaces 'If the team had followed', so the main clause must use 'would have' plus a past participle to express the imagined result. Learners often forget to switch to the perfect form after an inverted conditional.
translation: Якби команда уважніше дотримувалася інструкцій, проєкт був би завершений вчасно.
